questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage segment context. According to the text, why did the young boy decide to carry the injured sparrow inside his house?
options: A) He wanted to keep it in a cage as a permanent pet.
B) He noticed its broken wing and wanted to protect it from the approaching storm.
C) He wanted to show it to his friends at school.
D) He was asked by his mother to bring it inside.
questions.answer: B) He noticed its broken wing and wanted to protect it from the approaching storm.

questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage segment context. What did the boy use to create a comfortable temporary nest for the bird?
options: A) A wooden birdhouse with straw.
B) An old shoebox lined with soft cotton and cloth.
C) A plastic bowl filled with leaves.
D) A metallic cage with paper shreds.
questions.answer: B) An old shoebox lined with soft cotton and cloth.

questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage segment context. Choose the word from the passage which is the closest synonym for 'healed' or 'recovered'.
questions.answer: B) Mended

questions.question_text: Based on the unseen passage, why did the boy refuse to touch the bird's wing directly? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The boy refused to touch the wing directly because he knew it was fragile. He feared that applying too much pressure might cause the frightened bird more pain.

questions.question_text: How did the sparrow's behavior change on the third morning of its rescue? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: On the third morning, the sparrow was no longer shivering or hiding in the corner. It actively hopped around the box and eagerly chirped for its morning seeds.

questions.question_text: What important moral lesson does this short story teach us about human responsibility toward nature? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The story teaches us that humans have a moral responsibility to act with deep compassion and care toward vulnerable wildlife. Even a small act of kindness can save a life and restore balance in nature.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the type of sentence: 'Please pass me the salt from the kitchen counter.'
questions.answer: C) Imperative Sentence

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct abstract noun formed from the word 'brave': The soldier was rewarded for his extraordinary __________ on the battlefield.
questions.answer: C) bravery

questions.question_text: Choose the correct relative pronoun to complete the sentence: 'The girl __________ won the spelling bee competition is my best friend.'
questions.answer: B) who

questions.question_text: Select the correct degree of comparison to fill in the blank: 'Mount Everest is the __________ peak in the world.'
questions.answer: C) highest

questions.question_text: Fill in the blanks with the correct articles: 'I saw __________ elephant and __________ giraffe at the city zoo.'
questions.answer: B) an, a

questions.question_text: Identify the main verb in the following sentence and state its tense: 'The children were playing football in the rain.'
questions.answer: B) playing - Past Continuous Tense

questions.question_text: Choose the correct Subject-Verb Agreement: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers __________ present at the meeting yesterday.'
questions.answer: D) were

questions.question_text: Transform the given sentence into the Simple Future Tense: 'She writes beautiful poems.'
options: A) She has written beautiful poems.
B) She is writing beautiful poems.
C) She will write beautiful poems.
questions.answer: C) She will write beautiful poems.

questions.question_text: Write a short paragraph on the topic 'The Importance of Reading Books'. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Reading books is incredibly important because it expands our knowledge, improves our vocabulary, and enhances our imagination. When we read, we travel to different worlds and understand diverse perspectives. Books improve our focus, reduce daily stress, and ignite our creativity. Developing a daily reading habit makes us better thinkers and more empathetic individuals.

questions.question_text: Write a short diary entry expressing your feelings after winning the first prize in an inter-school debate competition. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Dear Diary, Today was an unforgettable day! I won the first prize in the inter-school debate competition. When the judges announced my name, my heart pounded with immense joy and pride. All my late-night research and practice finally paid off. My parents were beaming with happiness. I feel incredibly confident and motivated to participate in more events. Goodnight!

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'Paper Boats': 'Day by day I float my paper boats one by one down the running stream.' What does the child write on the boats?
options: A) A secret map to a hidden treasure.
B) His own name and the name of his village.
C) A poem about the beautiful flowing river.
D) A message to the stars in the sky.
questions.answer: B) His own name and the name of his village.

questions.question_text: According to the poem 'Try Again', what should a person do if they find their task is too hard and they fail initially?
options: A) Give up and find an easier task.
B) Wait for someone else to do it for them.
C) Persevere and keep trying without losing patience.
D) Complain about the difficulty of the task.
questions.answer: C) Persevere and keep trying without losing patience.

questions.question_text: In the story 'The Day the River Spoke', how did the river comfort the young girl when she felt lonely and misunderstood? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The river whispered gentle words of encouragement, reminding her that she was strong and capable. Its continuous, soothing flow gave her a deep sense of peace and inner confidence to face her struggles.

questions.question_text: In 'Animals Birds and Dr Dolittle', why did Dr. Dolittle decide to stop treating humans and become an animal doctor? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Dr. Dolittle realized that he preferred the company of animals over people. Once his parrot taught him animal languages, he discovered he could understand and treat their unique illnesses much better than human doctors.

questions.question_text: In Helen Keller's essay 'Three Days to See', what is the very first thing she wishes to see on her first day of sight? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Helen Keller wishes to see the faces of her dear friends and her teacher, Mrs. Anne Sullivan, whose kindness, patience, and companionship opened the outer world to her.

questions.question_text: In 'My Brothers Great Invention', what was the hilarious flaw in the brother's supposed "great invention" during his grand demonstration? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The hilarious flaw was that his elaborate, noisy machine, which he claimed would revolutionize chores, ended up just breaking a simple egg into a million pieces instead of cooking it properly.

questions.question_text: Helen Keller in 'Three Days to See' reminds us to appreciate our senses. Explain how her unique perspective teaches us to live life to the fullest. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Helen Keller teaches us to never take our physical senses for granted. Because she lacks sight and hearing, she deeply values every touch, smell, and visual beauty she imagines. She urges us to observe the world closely as if we might go blind tomorrow, inspiring immense gratitude for life's simple, everyday wonders.

questions.question_text: Describe the imaginative journey the child envisions for their boats in 'Paper Boats'. What does this tell us about the child's hopes? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The child imagines the paper boats floating to distant, unknown lands under the midnight stars, carrying shiuli flowers safely to the shore. This innocent vision reveals the child's deep sense of wonder, optimism, and hope that someone far away will find the boats and recognize who sent them.
